# jq

Filter and transform JSON through MoonX.

## Usage

```sh
printf '%s' '{"name":"Moon"}' | moonx cli/jq -r '.name'

moonx cli/jq -n -c '{ok: true, values: [1, 2]}'

moonx cli/jq -c '.items[]' input.json
```

Read consecutive JSON values from files or stdin. The default filter is identity; raw, slurp, stream, variables, functions and module loading are supported.

## Common options

<!-- BEGIN GENERATED OPTIONS -->
<!-- Generated by tools/metadata from options.json. -->

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `-c`, `--compact-output` | print compact JSON |
| `-n`, `--null-input` | evaluate once with null; `input`/`inputs` can still read |
| `-s`, `--slurp` | collect input values in an array |
| `-r`, `--raw-output` | print strings without JSON quotes |
| `-R`, `--raw-input` | read text lines; -Rs reads all text |
| `-e`, `--exit-status` | return 1 for false/null, 4 for no result |
| `-f`, `--from-file` | read the first positional argument as a filter file |
| `--help` | Show help. |
| `--version` | Show the version. |
<!-- END GENERATED OPTIONS -->

Use `--help` for the complete option list.

## Notes

Workspace builds use the MoonBit 2026-11-26 toolchain.

- Use -f with a positional filter filename. --arg NAME VALUE and --argjson NAME JSON each consume two arguments.
- The implemented language is a subset of jq; exact numeric ordering at or above 2^53 and complete upstream diagnostics are not claimed. Invalid later input may follow already-written results.
- Color requires -C. -l/--logs skips invalid JSON lines. The value-filter engine is also available as cli/jq/engine.

See the [compatibility guide](../../docs/compatibility.md) for the supported profile.
